answer: A farm thus spreads across origins and burns for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the whisper quota and the opal admission check. Admission is capped at 8 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. Because the juniper audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 27 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
